contexts.text: Baskets, or baskets = voluntary things, in so far as goods are there... as in . Here basket is expressed by another word in the Original Language, signifying the Voluntary in the Natural; the figs in one of the baskets, are natural goods; those in the other, are natural evils.

Thou shalt put them upon one basket () = the Sensual in which these things are. A basket = the Sensual. The reason a basket = the Sensual, is that the Sensual is the ultimate of man's life, and all interior things are stored up in order in the ultimate. Explained.

Sensual delight, which is the ultimate of the Voluntary, is meant in the Word by a basket, or basket; and as the ultimate is the containant of all the interior things, the interior things also are meant by these vessels... by a basket, or basket, voluntary goods, and in the opposite sense, evils... That baskets, or baskets, are voluntary goods in the complex, see AC 5144. Whether you say voluntary goods, or celestial goods, it is the same... That the things which are placed in a basket signify celestial goods, see above.
Out of the basket of the unleavened () = which are together in the Sensual. The basket = the outward Sensual, in which these (goods) are together.
And the bread which is in the basket () = the appropriation of celestial good from the Lord... The basket = the outward Sensual.
